progress.summary: Desktop-app initiative (Tauri 2 + Python sidecar) is the active thread: phases 1-2 complete and verified live on Windows (chat, thumbnail window picker, covered-window capture, hotkey, tray, single-instance, machine-wide config, unsigned MSI). Next: Windows acceptance matrix, code signing, then updater and fleet/MDM work. The macOS adapter is partially validated on Tahoe; desktop-UI rows, Retina, and secondary display still need a Mac.

platform.name: windows
platform.note: Adapter wraps existing Win32 modules; behavior unchanged.

platform.name: macos
platform.note: First hardware validation 2026-10-05 on macOS 26.6.2 (Tahoe, Mac mini M1, Hermes app as permission host). Working: TCC preflights, CGWindowList identity with titles, window-below chain, mss primary display, and window capture itself. Capture needed a code fix: the PyObjC 11.1 bindings lag macOS 26 (SCScreenshotConfiguration lost +configuration/pixelFormat; the framework selector walk raises NSInvalidArgumentException), so screenshot.py now layers a runtime accessor shim plus a CGWindowListCreateImage fallback (verified 673x439 exact). Blocked: the AXUIElement probe regressed mid-session after a probe process SIGABRT inside an AX XPC transaction; the AX AX server now returns self-referential degenerate windows to every Hermes-hosted process and System Events queries hang too. Believed to be wedged per-responsible-process AX state, not repo code (identical probe passed 08:35, failed 08:39, no code change). A Hermes relaunch is the pending remedy. Second session 2026-10-05 (after relaunch): AX wedge cleared and probe returned complete snapshots; TextEdit, Safari, Electron-class (Hermes), secure-field redaction, hung-provider timeout, stale- window bounded failure, permission preflights, and mss display capture all verified. A second wedge episode followed a hard kill of an AX-served test process; relaunch is the remedy again. Code fix: modal dialog panels (CGS layer 8) are now accepted capture targets by _is_candidate (was layer 0 only), with unit tests. Remaining: interactive TUI flow (backend request row), real-keypress hotkey row (pynput ignores injected events by design), Retina and secondary-display rows (hardware not available on the test machine).

initiative.name: desktop-app
initiative.note: Tauri 2 + React shell with PyInstaller Python sidecar. Working in live tauri-dev runs (2026-10-12): text-only chat, thumbnail window picker, PrintWindow capture of covered windows (blank detection + desktop-crop fallback with warning), submit against the real backend, single-instance enforcement, tray icon show/quit, hotkey chord in header, CWD-independent config resolution (env, cwd, exe dir, user dir) plus a machine-wide layer (%PROGRAMDATA%\LabGuide\labguide.toml) that wins per key so one file provisions every user of a machine. First MSI built: LabGuide_0.1.0_x64_en-US.msi (unsigned). Identity frozen: com.labguide.desktop / LabGuide / labguide-sidecar. Tests: 180 Python + 17 vitest. CSP enabled and verified rendering (2026-10-12). Real-keypress hotkey capture confirmed. Duplicated-transcript bug (StrictMode double-mount leaking event listeners) fixed twice: sync registration plus an attach() serialization race. Packaged UIA probe was silently broken (PyInstaller ignores -m); probe children now re-dispatch through the frozen entry. Accessibility extraction moved off the capture path (background merge + attachment.updated event; submit waits bounded) and ui_timeout_seconds default raised to 8s to cover bundled child startup. Backend health surfaced in the UI. README/example-config synced for the desktop app. Remaining: Authenticode cert + signed MSI, updater wiring, macOS bundle/notarization (needs a Mac), MDM confirmation with campus IT.

action.title: Windows acceptance pass for the desktop app
action.details: Run the existing matrix in docs/UI-Context-Capture-Execution-Plan.md against the desktop app (Notepad, standard error dialog, browser, elevated app, UIA timeout, secondary monitor), plus the sidecar robustness rows in docs/Desktop-App-Migration-Plan.md (crash mid-capture, slow sidecar, quit during probe, update with pending capture). Fix what it breaks. This closes the last functional acceptance item for Windows.
action.on-completion: Record outcomes in docs/UI-Context-Capture-Execution-Plan.md, mark Phase 5 acceptance done in the migration plan, update this file.

action.title: Code signing: Authenticode cert, then signed MSI
action.details: Procurement, not code: OV or EV code-signing certificate (EV avoids SmartScreen reputation lag). Then sign the shell and the sidecar with the same identity and rebuild the MSI. Required before any campus install. macOS notarization waits for a Mac.

action.title: macOS desktop validation on Tahoe, then bundle and notarize
action.details: Needs a Mac. Re-run the matrix in docs/Cross-Platform-Execution-Plan.md against the desktop app, close the Retina and secondary-display rows, and confirm the window picker (CGWindowList enumeration) on hardware. Then produce a signed, notarized app bundle with the sidecar inside it.

action.title: Fleet provisioning with campus IT (MDM)
action.details: Confirm the MDM system and push labguide.toml to %PROGRAMDATA%\LabGuide (Windows) / /Library/Application Support/ LabGuide (macOS). Decide the API-key policy for a machine-readable file. Add macOS TCC pre-approval profiles (Screen Recording, Accessibility) so users never see permission prompts.

action.title: Windows Graphics Capture (quality, not speed)
action.details: PrintWindow is fast (64 ms) but returns blank for some GPU-rendered windows; the desktop-crop fallback then shows whatever covers the target. WGC would fix that class of window. Deferred; not a performance item.

action.title: Tauri updater wiring
action.details: Needs updater signing keys. Start with a static update manifest; no update server to run. Static hosting plus a signed MSI is the prerequisite.

doc.role: proposed TUI-to-Tauri migration; fleet deployment requirements

invariants.invariant: Capture creates a local pending attachment; only explicit submit sends data.
Password/secure controls are redacted before serialization or logging.
Accessibility extraction runs in a child process with a parent-enforced hard timeout.
Screenshot-only and text-only paths must survive any accessibility failure.
OS API calls stay inside labguide.platforms adapters; PyObjC/pynput imports stay lazy.
Image and response size limits are enforced before request construction.
